title: Duplicate in Range
statement:
Find the one value that appears more than once in an array whose entries are all drawn from a small fixed range, without changing the array.

Contract
- `nums` has length `n + 1` and every entry is an integer from 1 to `n` inclusive (so `n >= 1`).
- Exactly one value occurs more than once; it may occur two times or many more times. Return that value.
- Do not modify `nums`, and do not sort it or copy it. Use only O(1) extra space.
- Inputs outside the contract (null, wrong length, entries out of range) are not tested.

Examples
- `findDuplicate([1, 3, 4, 2, 2])` returns `2`.
- `findDuplicate([3, 1, 3, 4, 2])` returns `3`.
- `findDuplicate([2, 2, 2, 2, 2])` returns `2`.
hints: A set or a counting array finds the repeat easily, and sorting does too, but the contract forbids extra memory and modifying the input.
Treat each index as a node whose single outgoing edge goes to the index `nums[i]`. Because there are n + 1 slots but only n possible targets, two slots lead to the same node.

Starting from index 0, the walk eventually enters a cycle, and the entry point of that cycle is the repeated value. Find the meeting point with a slow and a fast pointer, then restart one pointer at 0 and move both one step at a time until they meet. Intended complexity: O(n) time and O(1) space.
inputSyntax: Input: n+1 integers from 1..n with exactly one repeated value, for example: 3 1 3 4 2
